chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from al-Yasir al-Qummi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) who said:
The Fitrah (alms of breaking the fast) is one Sa' of wheat, or one Sa' of barley, or one Sa' of dates, or one Sa' of raisins; and it was Mu'awiyyah who lightened [the obligation] to wheat.

key_terms.صَاع: A traditional unit of volume measurement for dry goods
key_terms.فِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the alms tax given at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.مُعَاوِيَة: Mu'awiyyah ibn Abi Sufyan, noted for altering the measurement of Zakat al-Fitr

ai.seo_question: What are the permissible food items and quantities for Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) establishes the baseline quantities for Zakat al-Fitr using four staple foods, each measured as one Sa'. It provides historical context by attributing the reduction in the wheat obligation to Mu'awiyyah, reflecting the scholarly view that the original obligation was heavier or that Mu'awiyyah eased the burden for the people. This narration is central to the Shia jurisprudence of Zakat al-Fitr, emphasizing the Prophet's tradition while acknowledging historical administrative adjustments.
